stimulus.source_note: Photograph: The Beatles, 1964, by Bernard Gotfryd, public domain, via the Library of Congress and Wikimedia Commons. Audience figure verified against Smithsonian Magazine and the National Portrait Gallery.
stimulus.text:
The photograph, taken in 1964, shows the four members of the Beatles — John Lennon, Paul McCartney, George Harrison, and Ringo Starr — in four studio portraits against a gold curtain. All four wear dark suits and have the same mop-top haircut, with hair combed forward over their foreheads.

The Beatles first appeared on The Ed Sullivan Show on February 9, 1964. About 73 million Americans watched, the largest television audience to that date. Their appearance launched Beatlemania in the United States and opened the way for other British bands, a wave called the British Invasion.

stem: The photograph best shows which feature of the Beatles’ appeal to young Americans?

options.text: Their music copied the smooth crooning of their parents’ generation
options.misconception: Background: The Beatles built on rhythm and blues and rock ’n’ roll, not on their parents’ crooners.

options.text: Their matching suits and mop-top hair gave them a distinct youthful look
Their performances were aimed mainly at older, middle-aged audiences
options.misconception: Background: Their fans were famously young, not middle-aged.

options.text: Their popularity came mostly from radio play in Britain, not America
options.misconception: Their American television debut, not British radio, launched Beatlemania here.

rationales.A: Background: The Beatles drew on African-American rhythm and blues and rock ’n’ roll, not on the smooth crooning of their parents’ generation.
rationales.B: The photograph shows all four in matching dark suits with the same mop-top haircut, a look young fans could recognize and copy.
rationales.C: Background: The passage says about 73 million Americans watched them on Ed Sullivan, and their following was famously young.
rationales.D: The passage says their Ed Sullivan appearance launched Beatlemania in the United States.
rationales.general:
1. Look at the photograph: four young men, matching suits, matching mop-top hair.
2. That shared look was part of the act: fans could spot a Beatle at a glance.
3. The passage says their Ed Sullivan debut drew about 73 million viewers and launched Beatlemania.
4. A look that young fans could copy helped turn listeners into followers.
Remember: In pop culture, a shared look can be as much a message as a song.
